dimensions.assessment: Affects Indian tribes, the Department of the Interior, third parties seeking rights-of-way across tribal lands, and individuals or entities participating in tribal commercial activities.
dimensions.evidence: an Indian tribe may grant a right-of-way over and across the Tribal land of the Indian tribe for any purpose.

dimensions.assessment: Substantially alters how rights-of-way and leases are managed, shifting primary approval authority to tribes with approved regulations and exempting certain approvals from major federal environmental statutes.
dimensions.evidence: The Secretary of the Interior, in making an approval decision under this subsection, shall not be subject to--(i) the National Environmental Policy Act of 1969... (ii) section 306108 of title 54... or (iii) the Endangered Species Act of 1973

dimensions.assessment: Involves direct compensation and payments negotiated by Indian tribes, but no direct federal spending or revenue changes are specified.

Amends long-standing federal leasing and rights-of-way statutes (the Act of August 9, 1955, and the Act of February 5, 1948), creates new administrative pathways, and establishes tribal regulation review procedures.
dimensions.evidence: The Act of February 5, 1948... is amended... by adding at the end the following: SEC. 8. TRIBAL GRANTS OF RIGHTS-OF-WAY.

dimensions.assessment: Creates permanent structural changes in federal law regarding tribal land management, leasing terms, and rights-of-way approvals.

missing_information: The specific number of tribes expected to adopt independent regulations or the aggregate economic value of commercial leases and rights-of-way affected.
importance_detail.rationale: Modifies tribal leasing and rights-of-way authorities across Indian lands, allowing tribes to grant rights-of-way under approved tribal regulations with specific exemptions from federal environmental review statutes, while altering secretarial oversight and tribal jurisdiction.

other.label: CBO cost estimate: S. 3383, Unlocking Native Lands and Opportunities for Commerce and Key Economic Developments Act of 2025

summary: The Unlocking Native Lands and Opportunities for Commerce and Key Economic Developments Act of 2025 amends federal laws related to Indian land leasing and rights-of-way. Specifically, it expands leasing provisions for federally recognized tribes and permits Indian tribes to grant rights-of-way across their tribal land for any purpose without the direct approval of the Secretary of the Interior, provided they have an approved tribal regulation containing an environmental review process.

affected_groups.effect: Allowed to grant rights-of-way across tribal land independently of the Secretary of the Interior under approved tribal regulations, negotiate terms and compensation, and manage tribal land leasing and environmental review processes.

Granted authority to review, approve, or disapprove tribal regulations and rights-of-way documentation, handle compliance petitions, enforce or cancel rights-of-way at discretion, and exempted from specific federal environmental laws when approving regulations.

Provided opportunities to comment on significant environmental impacts identified by Indian tribes during tribal environmental reviews and permitted to submit compliance petitions to the Secretary of the Interior.

key_provisions: Amends the Long-Term Leasing Act to include land held in trust for any other Indian tribe on the most recent list published pursuant to the Federally Recognized Indian Tribe List Act of 1994.

Authorizes Indian tribes to grant rights-of-way across their tribal land for any purpose without needing the approval or grant of the Secretary of the Interior, if done under an approved tribal regulation.
Requires the Secretary of the Interior to approve or disapprove submitted tribal regulations within 180 days based on consistency with regulations and environmental review processes.

Exempts the Secretary of the Interior from the National Environmental Policy Act of 1969, section 306108 of title 54, and the Endangered Species Act of 1973 when making a regulation approval decision.

Provides that the United States is not liable for losses sustained by any party to a right-of-way granted by a tribe, though the Secretary may enforce or cancel rights-of-way under certain conditions.
Establishes a compliance petition process allowing interested parties to request Secretarial review of a tribe's compliance with its approved regulation after exhausting tribal remedies.
missing_information: The source text does not specify the precise volume of commerce, exact number of tribes affected, or economic dollar amounts involved.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Unlocking Native Lands and Opportunities for Commerce and Key Economic Developments Act of 2025 amends federal laws related to Indian land leasing and rights-of-way. Specifically, it expands leasing provisions for federally recognized tribes and permits Indian tribes to grant rights-of-way across their tribal land for any purpose without the direct approval of the Secretary of the Interior, provided they have an approved tribal regulation containing an environmental review process.
summary_detail.significance: This bill alters the administrative framework for leasing and granting rights-of-way on Indian trust and restricted lands by enabling tribes to manage rights-of-way directly through approved local regulations rather than obtaining individual federal approvals. The potential significance is scored at 50 because it modifies federal oversight procedures for tribal land commerce across federally recognized tribes.
